commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Stop sleep(level=2) from zeroing compressed-tensors KV scales
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`sleep(level=2)` zeroes the calibrated KV-cache scales of compressed-tensors
KV-FP8 checkpoints, so the first request after a weights-only reload — the shape an
RL weight-sync uses — returns **NaN logprobs and a wrong first token**.

Level 2 discards the weights allocation without keeping a copy, and the only
generic safety net is the `named_buffers()` snapshot in `Worker.sleep()` /
`Worker.wake_up()` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:253`, `:291`) — that file has no
`named_parameters` walk. `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading()`
rebinds `_q_scale`/`_k_scale`/`_v_scale` onto the `nn.Parameter` placeholders,
moving those names out of `_buffers`, so the snapshot never sees them and they come
back as blank pages reading `0.0`. `_prob_scale`, never rebound, survives — that
asymmetry pinpoints the cause, and every other KV-cache quant method is unaffected
because it `.copy_()`s into the existing buffer (`kv_cache.py:152/156/157/195`).

**Fix (+10/−3, one file):** `register_buffer()` the three scales — the form
`set_default_quant_scales(register_buffer=True)` created them in
(`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:129-135`). `register_buffer()`
rather than `.copy_()` because ATTN_HEAD loads `num_kv_heads` scales into a buffer
created 0-dim; `persistent=True` because `sharded_state_loader.py:162` needs the
keys. Shape, dtype, device, virtual address and the `state_dict` key set are
unchanged (measured: same keys, shapes and dtypes, 0 pointer moves). The single exit
covers TENSOR and ATTN_HEAD by measurement, MLA and the draft model statically (same
`_init_kv_cache_quant`, same buffers snapshotted) — we have not run MLA or
spec-decode.

We fixed the quant method rather than the snapshot because compressed-tensors is the
only one that breaks that buffer invariant; a worker-level `named_parameters()` net
would also cover the W8A8 case below, but it carries a host-memory cost and a policy
question, so it belongs in its own change.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs/issues for compressed-tensors KV scales, `sleep(level=2)`,
`_q/_k/_v_scale`, the `named_buffers` snapshot and `register_buffer`: nothing open
addresses this. Nearest hits #38975 (`_prob_scale_float` sync, no sleep involved)
and #55206 (release pinned host memory after `wake_up`). Related RFCs #48310, #48312.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py -k compressed_tensors_kv_scale
cd tests && VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v -s basic_correctness/test_mem.py
```

New case `test_deep_sleep_fp8_kvcache_compressed_tensors_kv_scale`, above the two
`…_mrv1` cases (the second builds its engine in the pytest parent and leaves its 0.9
KV pool mapped there, which a fork inherits). It asserts registration form, non-zero
values, exact equality with the pre-sleep copies, and greedy output/logprob parity
against a never-slept control, plus a `sleep(level=1)` negative control and an
anti-vacuity probe that the weights really were discarded and reloaded. Red arm =
revert only the fix. Exact equality is deliberate: an injected 4.657e-09
perturbation of these scales flipped a greedy decision at token 10.

Checkpoint `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor` (static
`kv_cache_scheme`, so the scales are genuinely calibrated; already used by
`tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py`). Measured floor 2.46 + 0.69 GiB, so
`gpu_memory_utilization=0.6` fits the `h200_18gb` slice this file runs on — no
`large_gpu_mark`, **not skipped in CI**.

## Test result (H20)

| arm | rc | result |
|---|---|---|
| pristine tree | **1** | `1 failed, 13 deselected, 17 warnings in 16.37s` — assertion names all 66 lost scales |
| with this fix | **0** | `1 passed, 13 deselected, 17 warnings in 23.18s` |
| with this fix, 10.8 GiB budget (≡ 18 GiB slice @ util 0.6) | **0** | `1 passed, 13 deselected, 17 warnings in 22.16s` |
| whole file as CI invokes it | **0** | `14 passed, 41 warnings in 221.09s` |

With the fix, output is **bit-exact against the never-slept control** (36/36 rounds,
324-tensor census 0 zeroed / 0 pointer moves), the noise floor is 0, and
`sleep(level=1)` is a clean negative control. Lint on the two changed files:
`ruff check` / `ruff format --diff` / `py_compile` clean and
`pre-commit run --files <both>` 13 Passed / 0 Failed — including
`check-forbidden-imports`, which is why the test resolves the hub id with the shared
`hf_api()` helper.

<details>
<summary>Full characterization on the 8B checkpoint (96/96 scales, NaN logprobs, FLASHINFER, CUDA graphs, TP=2, ATTN_HEAD)</summary>

8B `nm-testing/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-KV-FP8-tensor-static_minmax`, greedy with
logprobs: unfixed, **96/96** parameter-form scales read back `0.0` while **0/32**
buffer-form did and all 34,560 logprobs are NaN; with the fix, **36/36 rounds
bit-exact** vs the reload-only control, 324-tensor census 0 zeroed / 0 pointer
moves. Noise floor 0 (no-sleep reload 36/36 bit-exact; 22 pre-sleep references
across 22 processes identical); `sleep(level=1)` clean (0/128 changed). FLASHINFER
reproduces it identically, so it is not backend-specific; with CUDA graphs on, wake
re-captures nothing; at TP=2 exactly those 96 names flip form; ATTN_HEAD (`[8,1,1]`)
covered; old-format `quant_method="fp8"` unaffected at these scales.

</details>

## Model evaluation

GSM8K, full 1319-question test set, vLLM's own harness
(`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` — `_build_gsm8k_prompts` / `get_answer_value` /
`_score_gsm8k`; 5-shot, greedy, `max_tokens=256`, seed 0) on
`nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor` with
`kv_cache_dtype=fp8`:

| arm | accuracy | invalid | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — never slept | 2.65% (35/1319) | 0.6% | — |
| B — level=2 → wake(weights) → weights-only reload → wake(kv_cache), **with fix** | 2.65% (35/1319) | 0.6% | **1319/1319 byte-identical output** |
| C — same sequence, **without fix** | **0.00% (0/1319)** | **100%** | 0/1319 |

Absolute accuracy is low because TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat is weak at 5-shot GSM8K; the
signal is that B reproduces A byte-for-byte while C collapses (all 66
`_q/_k/_v_scale` read back `0.0`, every response runs to `max_tokens`, most decoding
to an empty string). Both sleeping arms assert the weights pool really was discarded
and the reload really restored 135 parameters bit-exactly, so the delta can only
come from the scales. A 500-question subset gave the same picture (500/500).

## Scope

The documented level-2 recovery -- `collective_rpc("reload_weights")` -- self-heals, and
this PR does not claim otherwise: the layerwise path re-creates the `k_scale`/`v_scale`
placeholders before replaying the checkpoint, so `process_weights_after_loading()` runs
again (measured: green with and without the fix). What does not self-heal is anything
that skips it: `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` with no reload at all,
`reload_weights(is_checkpoint_format=False)` (the kernel-format branch, `param.copy_()`
only, next to the `# TODO: buffers?`), and a third-party `model.load_weights()`. There
the `named_buffers()` snapshot is the only net, which is the level-2 contract in
`docs/features/sleep_mode.md` ("the model's buffers are kept in CPU") and the invariant
`test_static_model_tensors_survive_level2_restore` asserts at the same point. Measured
matrix and the exact reason a plain reload cannot restore them: follow-up comment.

## Platforms

Verified on CUDA/H20 only. The AMD mirror of `basic_correctness` collects this test
(`requires_fp8` is true on CDNA, sleep mode is available on MI3xx) and two assertions are
platform-sensitive: `discarded["all_zero"]`, which relies on the driver handing back zeroed
pages, and the bit-exact logprob comparison. If the mirror goes red we will relax those two
(tolerance / platform guard) and keep the buffer-form assertion, which is the point of the test.

## Not covered (disclosed)

- W8A8 `weight_scale` / `input_scale` are `nn.Parameter` too and are lost by the
  same mechanism: on `neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV`, **449 of 580**
  censused tensors read back `0.0` after level=2 + a weights-only reload (256
  weight/input scales, 129 weights, 64 norms), while its 128 KV/attention scales are
  buffers and survive. Needs the worker-level net above — separate change.
- The test pins `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, like the two adjacent `…_mrv1` cases.
  Both runners share `Worker.sleep()` and `_sleep_saved_buffers`, but we have not
  measured the V2 runner and do not claim it here.
- TP=2 shows a pre-existing per-engine output bimodality (2 of 24 snapshots; same
  signature with `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, also in the unfixed control arm) —
  unrelated to sleep or to this patch.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MiMo] Declare embedding_fields so an EPD pair can serve images
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58934.

This is my first contribution, so please let me know if there is anything I have to adjust!

### What

`MiMoV2OmniProcessingInfo.get_data_parser` now returns `MiMoV2OmniMultiModalDataParser` — a `Qwen2VLMultiModalDataParser` subclass declaring image fields only, built with MiMo's own `spatial_merge_size`, its 24 kHz audio target, `expected_hidden_size` and `allow_missing_mm_embeddings` — instead of the base `MultiModalDataParser`, which declares no `embedding_fields` at all.

The vision tower is Qwen2.5-VL-derived and the model already consumes `Qwen2_5_VLImageInputs` / `Qwen2_5_VLImageEmbeddingInputs`, splitting them with `grid_thw.prod(-1) // merge_size // merge_size`, so Qwen2-VL's field declaration (`image_embeds` = values, `image_grid_thw` = metadata) is the one it needs. Without it `collect_ec_item_metadata` publishes `metadata: {}`, the EPD proxy finds nothing to rewrite and forwards raw media to a `--language-model-only` decode server, where every modality limit is 0 and the request dies with `At most 0 image(s) may be provided in one prompt`.

### Why this is not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "58934 in:body"` → empty
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "MiMo embedding_fields"` → empty
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "MiMo EPD"` → empty
- `gh search issues --repo vllm-project/vllm "embedding_fields"` and `gh search prs ... "embedding_fields"` → no hit on a model declaring (or missing) these fields

The nearby EPD work (#52409 tracker, #50160, #50390, #51222) is about the connector and proxy plumbing itself; none of it covers MiMo's missing declaration.

## Test Plan

`prek`/`pre-commit` cannot install its hook toolchain in this environment (its bundled `uv` binary does not run on NixOS), so the two hooks that apply to this file were run directly with `ruff`:

```
ruff check vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2_omni.py     # All checks passed
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2_omni.py  # 1 file already formatted
```

No `.venv` could be built here, so `pytest tests/multimodal/test_parse.py` ran inside the vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev449+geb8798058` serving container:

```
with this change:    8 failed, 18 passed
with the change reverted (same container, same tests):  8 failed, 18 passed
```

`tests/multimodal/test_embedding_shape_validation_unit.py`: 18 passed, 0 failed.

## Test Result

Only the image path got end-to-end testing on my side; audio and video didn't.

Identical either way: the 8 failures in `test_parse.py` are all `test_audio_metadata_*`, which fail inside `assert_never` on `audio_num_tokens` — a field today's `main` tests use and this build does not implement — and that file never references MiMo.

No benchmark eval was run: the pre-change baseline rejects every image request with HTTP 400, so there is no comparable score. Serving was verified end to end on a real EPD deployment (encoder-only producer on one GPU, `--language-model-only` consumer on two, `ECExampleConnector` over shared storage): before the change the encoder answered 200, the proxy logged no rewrite and decode answered 400; after it, the proxy logs `Rewrote 1 media item(s) as metadata references` and decode answers 200.

## AI Assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (pi coding agent); the submitting human reviewed the diff and is accountable for it.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Profile maximum DeepSeek V4.1 vision features
commits.pr_body:
# [Bugfix] Profile the largest legal DeepSeek V4.1 image patch grid

## Purpose

The profiling dummy assumes a square maximizes vision features. The image-token
budget includes one newline token per LLM row, however:
`tokens = rows * (columns + 1) + 2`. A wider legal image can spend less of the
budget on newlines and produce more ViT patches than the square dummy.

With the Flash defaults (patch 14, downsample 3, budget 1024):

| Image | Size (width x height) | ViT patches | Image-span tokens |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Previous dummy | 1302 x 1302 | 8649 | 994 |
| Legal wide image | 2814 x 630 | 9045 | 1022 |
| New dummy | 42882 x 42 | 9189 | 1024 |

Enumerate LLM row counts, maximize the patch grid under the token budget and
optional aspect-ratio clamp, and avoid the minimum-pixel upscaler changing the
chosen aspect ratio. Runtime image preprocessing is unchanged.

Per review, the mock-based test file has been removed from this PR. Only the
profiling selector change remains; its implementation is unchanged. The earlier
validation covered budgets 64/256/512/1024 and six aspect-ratio configurations,
compared against independently enumerated legal grids, and included the
default-wide-image regression.

## Duplicate Work

On 2026-09-21, searches for open PRs matching `DeepSeek image profiling` and
`"DeepSeek" "most_features"` found no equivalent fix.

## Validation Results

The results below were collected before the test-file removal. No new GPU or
serving run is claimed for this review update. Applicable pre-commit hooks
(including Ruff and mypy) and `git diff --check` passed after the removal.

Base: `3c84ad13ed3f9fcd816bf1d15acb83c28cfa02f9`.

- Focused tests on unchanged main: 24 failures, 1 pass.
- Fixed CPU source with real PIL/torch: 25 passed.
- Both originally modified files passed applicable pre-commit hooks.
- The installed H20 runtime passes all 25 image-processor regressions; the
  combined installed-code suite passes 74 tests (including 46 CUDA/Triton cases).
- Restarted the real Flash TP8 H20 service: encoder profiling completed with
  eight maximum-feature images, and the service became healthy. Identical
  serial HTTP tests passed 10/10 before and after, with 5/5 additional unbiased
  image/color/counting checks passing after restart. Runtime: vLLM
  `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9`, torch `2.13.0+cu130`, real Flash weights,
  TP8+EP and DSpark (5 draft tokens, adaptive verification disabled).
  The original target module is byte-for-byte identical to the main base above.

## Previous Test Commands

The removed test file remains available in the
[pre-removal commit](https://github.com/xijiaat/vllm/blob/cec835cc67de537651594583991fc2e438c98fc2/tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_v41.py).
The following command was run with that file present; it is not a test command
for the current PR head:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_v41.py -q
```

On H20, the harness invoked `pytest.main` on this staged file with
`--confcutdir=tests -o addopts= -p no:cacheprovider`, against the actual installed
module. All 25 image regressions passed. The combined suite also included the
separate Engram revision fix and its existing CUDA kernels: 74 passed, 38
deselected, one unknown distributed-marker warning from isolation of conftest.

Real-service smoke: 4 text cases, square/wide/extremely-wide/portrait image
requests, text and image SSE with usage and DONE; then 4 unbiased color questions
and one streamed shape-counting question. All 15 post-restart cases passed.
Both proposed fixes were installed for this integration run; only the profiling
selector change remains in this PR. Requests were serial, capped at
128 output tokens. This is smoke coverage, not a comprehensive accuracy or
throughput benchmark. No generated/random model weights were used for serving.

## Scope and Accountability

The change was developed with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex). The submitting human
has reviewed the changes and confirmed personally rerunning the relevant tests
for these new fixes successfully. Automated test results above were also
collected by the assistant; the submitter's confirmation is separate.

Patch-count underestimation is demonstrated. It is not equivalent to the same
percentage increase in GPU memory. Baseline wide-image HTTP requests succeeded
on the H20 test service; no baseline GPU OOM has been reproduced. This is a
profiling coverage fix, not a demonstrated fix for production OOM, deadlock,
or generation-quality incidents.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CI] Assert the logger call the Anthropic merge warning makes
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`TestDetectMergeInlineSystem::test_probes_resolved_template_without_cli_override`
has been failing on main since #59172. Failing job: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13788

That PR changed a single line in `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`, turning the inline-system merge warning from `logger.warning` into `logger.warning_once` so it is not repeated on every request. It did not touch the test.

The test replaces the whole module logger with a `MagicMock` and then asserts:

```python
assert mock_logger.warning.called is expected
```

The mock records the call under `warning_once`, so `warning.called` stays `False`. Only the parametrization that expects a warning fails; the permissive-template case passes by coincidence, since both the expectation and the recorded value are
`False`.

## Test

`pytest -q entrypoints/anthropic` now reports `93 passed`, the same 93 tests the
failing job ran with one of them red.

commits.pr_title: [MM] Fix compiled ViT attention output layouts
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
Fix a `torch.compile` stride mismatch in the custom attention operations used by multimodal vision encoders.

The fake implementations previously returned `torch.empty_like(q)`, which advertised that each operation's output inherited Q's strides. That is not a valid contract: FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton attention, and PyTorch SDPA allocate or produce their outputs independently, and their output layout can differ from a non-contiguous Q view.

This was found while enabling `compile_mm_encoder` for Mistral3's Hugging Face Pixtral vision encoder (#57168). Its RoPE path transposes Q/K from BSHD to BHSD and back before attention. On PyTorch 2.14, Inductor can remove the caller-side `.contiguous()` conversion, exposing the mismatch between the fake and real custom-op output layouts.

Reproducer using pre-fix vLLM, PyTorch 2.13, and CUDA:

```python
import torch

from vllm.v1.attention.ops.vit_attn_wrappers import vit_flash_attn_wrapper


@torch.compile(fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)
def compiled_attention(q, k, v):
    return vit_flash_attn_wrapper(
        q.transpose(1, 2).contiguous(),
        k.transpose(1, 2).contiguous(),
        v.transpose(1, 2).contiguous(),
        batch_size=1,
        is_rocm_aiter=False,
        fa_version=None,
    )


shape = (1, 16, 4960, 64)  # BHSD
q = torch.randn(shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
k = torch.randn_like(q)
v = torch.randn_like(q)
compiled_attention(q, k, v)
```

Expected result:

```text
AssertionError: expected size 4960==4960, stride 64==1024 at dim=1;
expected size 16==16, stride 317440==64 at dim=2
Error in op: torch.ops.vllm.flash_attn_maxseqlen_wrapper.default
```


### Changes

- Make all four fake implementations advertise a newly allocated contiguous BSHD output.
- Guarantee the same layout from the real FlashAttention, Triton, SDPA, and FlashInfer wrappers.
- Add registered-op fake-tensor coverage for all layout contracts and a real GPU test for SDPA without sequence metadata.

## Test Plan
Focused layout-contract tests for the fake ops:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_vit_attn_wrappers.py -q
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Force reasoning mode for GLM-5.3 chat templates in the GLM MoE parser
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #54744.

GLM-5.3 keeps the GLM-4.x prompt and tool-call format but replaces the `enable_thinking` toggle with an always-on `"Reasoning Effort:"` header. The template's generation prompt unconditionally appends `<|assistant|><think>`, so the model output carries no opening `<think>` tag and thinking cannot be turned off. When a client passes `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` (or `"thinking": false`, honored by GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7 templates), the `Glm47MoeParser` disabled reasoning extraction while the model still thought, leaking the whole scratchpad into `message.content` and reporting an empty reasoning field. It also made `is_reasoning_end()` return `True` immediately, so structured-output constraints applied from token 0 while the model was still reasoning.

The fix detects the GLM-5.3 template signature on the tokenizer (`[gMASK]<sop>` + `Reasoning Effort:` + no `enable_thinking` + GLM tool-call tags, the same predicate SGLang uses) in `Glm47MoeParser.__init__` and discards the thinking-disable kwargs with a one-time warning. The parser then builds the thinking-armed engine config (`initial_state=REASONING`), so streaming, non-streaming, and `is_reasoning_end` paths all behave exactly as they do today for requests without the kwarg. GLM-4.5–4.7 templates declare `enable_thinking` and are untouched (pinned by a negative-control test).

## Why this is not a duplicate

Two open PRs touch the same symptom with materially different approaches:

- #54276 nulls only the `enable_thinking` kwarg when the template lacks it. A client sending `thinking: false` still leaks, and the loose `"enable_thinking" not in template` check is replaced here by the positive GLM-5.3 family signature ported from SGLang.
- #54825 splits leaked think blocks post-hoc in non-streaming extraction and explicitly leaves streaming broken. Fixing the config at construction time (this PR) covers streaming, non-streaming, tool calling, and the structured-output `is_reasoning_end` gate in one place.

## Test commands and results

- `pytest tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py -q` — 20 passed (16 existing + 4 new: both kwarg names forced, streaming split, GLM-4.7 negative control). The three force-tests fail on current main as expected.
- `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py -q` — 13 passed.
- `pytest tests/reasoning/ -q` — 436 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on both touched files; pre-commit hooks passed on the commit.

## Model evaluation (GLM-5.3-Flash, 8xH100, TP8+EP, MTP k=5)

A/B against unpatched main, same launch flags (`--reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47`):

| Request | main (unpatched) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`, non-stream | reasoning empty; content = scratchpad + `"4"` (leak) | reasoning parsed, content = `"4"` |
| `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": false}`, non-stream | same leak | reasoning parsed, content = `"4"` |
| no kwargs (control) | correct | identical behavior |
| `enable_thinking: false` + stream | leak | reasoning deltas then content delta, 15 deltas |
| `enable_thinking: false` + tool call | — | `finish_reason=tool_calls`, `get_weather({"city": "Paris"})`, reasoning parsed |

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Support strict MiMo-V2.6 tool calling
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

MiMo-V2.6 Pro/Flash emit compact XML tool calls, but `--tool-call-parser mimo` currently selects Qwen3-Coder structural tags with mandatory newlines. Strict required/named calls therefore use the wrong wire format. The Qwen argument converter also removes a leading/trailing newline that MiMo emits as part of the string value.

Introduce a MiMo variant of the existing parser engine that preserves parameter whitespace, with a thin tool adapter selecting `mimo` structural tags. Prefer the new XGrammar builtin (https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/pull/916); keep a schema-constrained compatibility builder for the currently pinned 0.2.7 wheel. Honor `parallel_tool_calls=False`, retain server/per-tool strictness controls, and leave reasoning to the serving gate. No dependency change is required.

The shared registry change only declares the supported key. MiMo parsing and compatibility behavior live in the model's own modules. Document the existing `--tool-call-parser mimo --reasoning-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice` flags and strictness options.

Duplicate-work check: open #54393 and #57933 add Rust frontend MiMo support. This PR changes the Python parser/structural-tag path; neither existing PR covers it. Also searched open MiMo/XGrammar/strict-tool PRs before submission.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3_reasoning.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py --tb=short
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

The local environment used the current checkout plus an isolated XGrammar build. Repeated MiMo cases with the actual 0.2.7 wheel first on `PYTHONPATH`. Supplemental replay loads revision-pinned official tokenizers, renders chat-template completions, checks each native token mask and EOS boundary, and parses the resulting calls in both non-streaming and token-streaming modes.

## Test Result

commits.pr_title: [Docs] Speed up docs build ~5x
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The docs build on Read the Docs has grown from ~11 min in March to ~33 min today (median `latest` build duration from the RTD API). The growth is steady rather than a single regression because the dominant cost scales with `pages x nav size`, and the API reference adds to both every time a module is added.

This PR makes the build ~5x faster (539s -> 107s locally) in three commits:

1. **Prune the API reference navigation.** Every page embedded the full nav, ~3150 items and ~650KB of HTML, of which the API reference is the overwhelming majority. Material's [`navigation.prune`](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/setting-up-navigation/#navigation-pruning) fixes this, but only globally. Instead, `docs/mkdocs/overrides/partials/nav.html` overrides Material's `nav.html` to render only the API reference section with pruning, so the rest of the nav is unchanged. On API pages, the active path stays expanded and sibling modules are collapsed (loaded on navigation via `navigation.instant`).
2. **Remove `mkdocs-minify-plugin`.** HTML minification (pure Python `htmlmin`) was the largest remaining cost (~44% in a profile). It shrinks the raw output, but the compressed size (what the RTD CDN actually serves) only grows by ~9% without it.
3. **Upgrade docs dependencies.** Notably `mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin` 1.6.0, which caches the per-page `git tag --points-at` lookups (~13% of the remaining build time), plus newer `mkdocstrings-python`, `griffelib`, `pymdown-extensions`, etc. `mkdocs-material` 9.7.6 -> 9.7.7 does not change `nav.html` or `nav-item.html`, so the override is still in sync (it links to the upstream template it is based on for easy comparison).

## Results

Local `mkdocs build` (non-strict), each commit built sequentially from a clean worktree with its own `requirements/docs.txt` synced. Time is the `Documentation built in` value reported by mkdocs; gzip is the size of the site directory as a `.tar.gz`.

| Commit | Build time | Site size | Site size (gzip) | `index.html` | `api/vllm/config/index.html` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base (`main`) | 539s | 2026MB | 184MB | 651KB | 6.54MB |
| 1. Prune API nav | 257s (-52%) | 634MB | 97MB | 97KB | 6.01MB |
| 2. Remove minify | 179s (-30%) | 965MB | 106MB | 179KB | 6.61MB |
| 3. Upgrade deps | 107s (-40%) | 965MB | 107MB | 179KB | 6.61MB |
| **Total** | **-80%** | **-52%** | **-42%** | **-72%** | |

RTD builders are slower than my machine (base is ~33 min there vs ~9 min locally), so the absolute savings on RTD should be proportionally larger.

## Duplicate check

No open PRs touch the docs build performance, `navigation.prune`, the minify plugin or the docs requirements (searched `docs build`, `mkdocs`, `navigation.prune`, `minify`).

## Test Plan

```bash
uv pip sync requirements/docs.txt
mkdocs build -f mkdocs.yaml
```

## Test Result

All four builds succeed and emit the same single warning (`griffe: vllm/model_executor/layers/fusion/mm_input_norm.py:85: No type or annotation for returned value 1`). It comes from the base commit and is already fixed on `main`. None of these commits add warnings.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Account for new requests in DP routing
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The routing score `max(inflight, running + waiting)` can remain unchanged
across successive admissions when the scheduler snapshot exceeds local
inflight counts. After cancellations reduce local inflight, a burst can
therefore concentrate on one engine before updated stats arrive.

For example, with fixed scheduler loads of 10 and 12 and zero local
inflight requests, 14 consecutive admissions produce a 13/1 split.

Track admissions since the latest scheduler snapshot and include them in
the load estimate. Reset this delta whenever a new snapshot arrives,
retaining local inflight as a lower bound. Each admission then immediately
increases the selected engine's score, producing an 8/6 split in the example.

Both automatic and explicitly targeted requests update the estimate.
Existing tie-breaking and explicit rank selection remain unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] MiMo: keep fused fp8 qkv_proj pairing state across weight-loading calls
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
`XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL` (and V2.5) produce degenerate output when using `--load-format fastsafetensors` or `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` when testing on Mi355x.  This issue should be platform-agnostic. 

## Root cause

MiMo's fused fp8 `qkv_proj` arrives as two checkpoint tensors (`weight` and `weight_scale_inv`) that must be sharded together, so `MiMoV2Model.load_weights` paired them in a dict and flushed only when both members arrived in the *same* call.

`AutoWeightsLoader._groupby_prefix` (`vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:260-274`) groups the stream with `itertools.groupby` on the first name component and calls a child's `load_weights` **once per contiguous run of `model.*`**. Any pair that straddles a group boundary therefore never flushes and both parameters are left uninitialised — zeros/NaN for the fp8 weight and `-inf` for its scale:

Instrumented load (`mimo_v2.py`), TP=2:

| loader | `layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight` | `…weight_scale_inv` |
|---|---|---|
| default | correct | correct |
| `--load-format fastsafetensors` | `sum=0` | `sum=-inf` |
| `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` | `sum=0`/`NaN` | `sum=-inf` |

`eager` fragments heavily because `safetensors.torch.load` returns a Rust `HashMap` (not file order). Nothing errored because weights tracking is disabled for quantized models (`default_loader.py:435-438`), hence gibberish tokens instead of a load failure.

## Fix

MiMo's fused fp8 `qkv_proj` arrives as two separate tensors — the weight and its scale — which have to be sharded together, so the loader holds the first one until the second shows up. That holding area was a local variable, and a local variable only lives for one call of `load_weights`; when the loader runs more than once (fastsafetensors, eager), a pair can be split across two calls, both tensors are dropped, and the attention projections are left empty.

Keep the holding area on the model instead (`mimo_v2.py`, and the same spot in `mimo_v2_mtp.py`), so a pair still completes no matter which call each half arrives in. Nothing in the loader itself is changed, so no other model is affected.

## Test Plan
Start serving with this, change model id to `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` and add `--load-format fastsafetensors` or `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` when testing the different case. 
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --generation-config vllm \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
  --tool-call-parser mimo \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser mimo
```

Test with lmeval, change model id to `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` for the mimo v2.5 test. 
```
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \  
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template
```

## Test Result

| MiMo V2.6, default loader |  gsm8k @ 25 shots (~0.97)  |
| MiMo V2.6, `--load-format fastsafetensors` | gsm8k @ 25 shots (~0.97) |

commits.pr_title: [Feat][Model] Enable KDA prefill checkpoints for GLM-5.3-Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
 Enable KDA prefill checkpoints for GLM-5.3-Flash.


## Problem

  GLM-5.3-Flash already supports prefix caching. However, in
  `mamba-cache-mode=align`, its KDA implementation currently persists
  states at the end of a prefill chunk.

  To preserve a reusable state at a cache boundary inside the input,
  the scheduler may split the prefill at that boundary and process
  the remaining tokens in another iteration. This introduces an
  additional scheduling iteration and model forward, potentially
  with a very small trailing chunk.

see `_mamba_block_aligned_split`


  For example, when a 1159-token prompt requires a cached state at
  token 1152, prefill may be split into 1152 tokens followed by
  7 tokens, even when the token budget allows processing the entire
  prompt in one iteration.

  ## Solution

  Reuse the KDA prefill checkpoint mechanism already implemented
  for Kimi K3 and enable it for GLM-5.3-Flash with FlashKDA.

  The implementation:
  - Advertises support for an internal prefill checkpoint through
    the GLM KDA cache specification.
  - Passes the checkpoint offset to FlashKDA to export the recurrent
    state while processing the full prefill.
  - Saves the corresponding convolution history alongside that state.
  - Shares checkpoint metadata construction and cache-storage code

## Purpose

Enable device-side image rescaling and normalization for:

- `LlamaNemotronVLForEmbedding`
- `LlamaNemotronVLForSequenceClassification`

This extends the device-side normalization infrastructure introduced in #50411 to Llama Nemotron VL's SigLIP vision encoder. The sequence-classification model inherits the embedding model's multimodal processing path, so both models use the same implementation.

Previously, the custom processor always rescaled and normalized images on the CPU and transferred float32 pixel tensors to the GPU. With this change, a supported device-normalization request leaves pixels as `uint8` on the CPU, transfers the smaller tensor, and performs the SigLIP rescaling and normalization on the device immediately before the vision encoder.

### Performance

Benchmark environment:
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti 8 GB
- Intel Core i9-10920X
- PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
- BF16 vision inputs
- one CPU intra-op thread
- dynamic tiling with up to six 512x512 tiles plus a thumbnail
- renderer: median of 30 iterations after five warmups
- executor: median of 100 CUDA-event measurements after ten warmups
- executor timing excludes the vision encoder and measures pinned H2D transfer plus dtype conversion/device normalization

Results:

| Input     | Tiles | CPU renderer | Device renderer | Renderer speedup | CPU executor | Device executor | Executor speedup | H2D payload       |
|-----------|------:|-------------:|----------------:|-----------------:|-------------:|----------------:|-----------------:|------------------:|

commits.pr_title: [Model] Decoder-side SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Decoder-side SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1, on top of the encoder side (#56227). The layers past the last KV-source layer (21-39 of 40 on V4.1-Flash) own only sliding-window KV, so in eager prefill steps they run on each request's last 128 tokens, cold prefills included. Simplified re-submission of #56752 (closed); no other open PR implements this.

- `DeepseekV41ModelState.prepare_attn` prepares the kept rows as a sub-batch, the way a microbatch is prepared: one Triton kernel gathers rows, positions, slot mappings and the replay-layer KV start, and the sub-batch gets attention metadata and a forward context of its own. DP ranks agree on whether any rank trims and on every rank's replay token count.
- `DecoderReplayLayers` gathers the layer inputs by those rows, runs the replay layers under that context and scatters the outputs back.
- Only eager steps trim. A step that fits a CUDA graph (up to 1024 tokens by default) keeps the replay layers on its whole batch inside the graph: such steps are launch-bound, so the graph is worth more than the trim. `prepare_attn` already gets the step's graph mode, which DP ranks share, so there are no nested captures, no eager breaks and no runner changes; the diff is confined to `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/`, a config docstring and the CI job list.
- With the fused MoE finalize of #58586, a decode step's cut layer hands its unfinalized `MoEOutput` to the replay layers unchanged, and layer 21's first boundary finalizes it. A trimming step holds a prefill longer than the window, more tokens than any step that defers its finalize, so the trim path only sees tensors.
- Stays off, with a warning, when the PP stage does not hold every layer after the cut, under sequence-parallel MoE, PCP or microbatching, with an Engram layer after the cut, or with a drafter window wider than the target's. `--no-swa-bounded-replay` turns off both sides. A no-op on ROCm.

## Test Plan

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Support raise_exception in chat templates
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59009.

The Rust frontend renders HF chat templates with minijinja, which does not define `raise_exception`, the helper [transformers injects](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py) into chat templates. Templates that use it to reject unsupported input, such as Qwen3.8 rejecting `reasoning_effort: "high"`, failed with `unknown function: raise_exception is unknown` and returned HTTP 500, which clients retry. The reporter's agent client retried in a loop.

Register `raise_exception` so it fails the render with the template's own message, and surface that as a new `ChatTemplateRejected` request-validation error. The existing `chat_submit_error` then returns 400 `invalid_request_error` with the template's message, matching the Python frontend's `TemplateError` → 400 mapping in `vllm/entrypoints/serve/exception_handling/error_response.py`.

Other template failures (e.g. an unknown function from a template typo) still return 500. Python returns 400 for every `TemplateError`; happy to widen this if you prefer full parity.

## Test Plan

```sh
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
pre-commit run --all-files
```

New tests cover the template's message passing through, an untaken raise_exception branch still rendering, unknown functions staying 500, and the 400 mapping in server/src/error.rs.

Test Result

- Full Rust workspace: 1894 passed, 13 skipped; clippy and pre-commit clean.
- The new tests fail with the raise_exception registration removed.
- No model evaluation needed: rendering output is unchanged for templates that don't raise. The reporter offered to verify on their 2x4090 Qwen3.8 setup.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Model][Bugfix] Fix GLM-5.2 shared-expert fusion and MTP on the ROCm DSA path
commits.pr_body:
#51915 aliased `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` onto `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/`. That enabled GLM-5.2-MXFP4 there, but it also moved GLM-5.2-FP8 onto a path missing two things the model needs, so the AMD command from the [GLM-5.2 recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/zai-org/GLM-5.2) now fails twice on ROCm:

1. **`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` can't load the checkpoint** — `KeyError: 'layers.10.mlp.shared_experts.down_proj.weight'`. With fusion on, the checkpoint gives one widened `mlp.shared_experts` tensor per layer. `deepseek_v2.py` splits it into the expert slots appended after the routed experts, but `DeepseekV32Model` subclasses `torch.nn.Module` rather than `DeepseekV2Model`, reimplements `load_weights`, and has no equivalent handling.

2. **MTP kills the engine on the first request** — `AttributeError: 'DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor' object has no attribute 'compact_topk_indices'`. `llm_base_proposer` calls that method once `index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is set, which GLM-5.2's config sets. `nvidia/mtp.py` implements it; `amd/mtp.py` never did.

Before #51915, GLM-5.2 fell through to the generic `deepseek_v2` implementation on ROCm, which handles both. This adds the missing pieces rather than changing the routing, so MXFP4 keeps the AMD path.

## Changes

- `amd/model.py`: set `is_fused_shared_expert_enabled`, size the expert params mapping to `n_routed_experts + n_shared_experts`, and split the widened shared-expert tensor into `mlp.experts.{n_routed_experts + j}` — dim 0 for the ColumnParallel gate/up, dim 1 for the RowParallel down. Ported from `deepseek_v2.py` to keep both paths consistent.
- `amd/mtp.py`: add `compact_topk_indices`, matching `nvidia/mtp.py`. The ROCm attention already maintains `skip_topk` and `topk_indices_buffer`, so it ports over unchanged.

## Test Plan

8x MI325X (gfx942), `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`, recipe AMD command unmodified (fusion on, 5-token MTP on). Baseline `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` at `0.30.1rc1.dev143+g29468dde8`; patched run is the same image with these two files replaced.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter
```

## Test Result

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Weight loading | `KeyError` at `layers.10` | completes |
| KV cache @ 524288 | n/a | 1,668,416 tokens, 3.18x concurrency |
| First request | `AttributeError`, engine dies | returns normally |
| MTP | unusable | active, mean acceptance length 3.41 |

Correctness checked too, since a bad tensor split would give fluent-but-wrong output rather than an error: `17 * 23` → `391`, capital of Peru → `Lima`, `Is 91 prime?` → 822 chars of reasoning then the correct 7 x 13, and a correct three-sentence Rayleigh-scattering answer with `enable_thinking: false`. The `glm47` parsers behave as before.

I only have gfx942, so MI300X and MI355X are untested — the changed code is shared ROCm model code with no gfx-specific branching, but an MI355X run from someone would be welcome. MXFP4 on the AMD path is untouched here but likewise unverified.

commits.pr_title: [DSv4.1] Avoid runtime recompiles of _ring_slot_mapping_kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`_ring_slot_mapping_kernel` builds the compressor ring slot mapping in `CompressorMetadataBuilder.build()` and runs on every step. Its int args `num_tokens` and `num_actual_tokens` change from step to step, and Triton specializes int args by value (`== 1`, `% 16 == 0`, or neither), so each new combination compiles a new variant while serving. These compiles are not covered by startup warmup because the triggering combinations depend on the live batch (for example, a real token count that is a multiple of 16 padded to one that is not). Under DP/EP, a rank that stops to compile stalls every other rank at the next collective.

This PR marks `block_table_stride`, `num_actual_tokens` and `num_tokens` as `do_not_specialize`, so one variant is compiled at startup and reused for every batch. These args only feed address and mask arithmetic; dropping their divisibility hints narrows some loads/stores, but the kernel is latency-bound on its dependent loads and performance is unchanged (see below).

Evidence from a DSv4.1-Flash DEP4 AgentX run on GB200: a new variant of this kernel was compiled 46 min after the server was healthy, in the middle of a benchmark, and the Triton cache holds 6 variants of it.

This does not overlap with #58560, which changes the kernel's store mask (null block), not its specialization.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py`
- Kernel microbenchmark: main (bare `@triton.jit`) vs this PR on GB200, FlashInfer `bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` (CUPTI), `block_table_stride=1` and `CAPACITY=8` (5 draft tokens) as in serving. 37 token counts from 1 to 8192, exact and padded; outputs match exactly.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Hoist $defs/definitions in Cohere parser tool schema composition
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a bug where any `/v1/chat/completions` request with tools whose JSON Schema
contains `$defs`/`definitions` fails with HTTP 500 on Cohere models served with
`--reasoning-parser cohere_command3|cohere_command4`.

Resolves the bug class reported in #16467 (closed as stale, never fixed) for the
Cohere reasoning parser path specifically. Other parsers that compose their own
grammars are out of scope (see the GLM case in #47175); the generic tool path in
`vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` already hoists `$defs` and is unaffected.

**Root cause.** `collect_tool_schema` in
`vllm/reasoning/cohere_command_reasoning_parser.py` builds the constrained-decoding
grammar for tool calls by nesting each tool's `parameters` schema inside a
`{tool_call_id, tool_name, parameters}` envelope. The tool schema was spliced in
verbatim, so a definitions block originally at the schema root ends up under
`properties.parameters`, while its `$ref` pointers (`#/$defs/X`) remain
root-anchored. xgrammar then correctly rejects the dangling JSON pointer:

```text
RuntimeError: Cannot find field $defs in #/$defs/X
```

The request fails during preprocessing, before generation. Agentic frameworks such as pydantic-ai emit `$defs`
for any nested model, so this breaks effectively all tools defined via such
frameworks (see user reports in #16467).

**Minimal repro** against a Cohere model served with
`--reasoning-parser cohere_command4 --tool-call-parser cohere_command4 --enable-auto-tool-choice`
(any tool schema whose parameters carry `$defs` + `$ref`; a flat schema without
`$defs` does not reproduce):

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Weather in Prague?"}],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "parameters": {
          "$defs": {
            "Location": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "city": {"type": "string"},
                "country": {"type": "string"}
              },
              "required": ["city"]
            }
          },
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"location": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Location"}},
          "required": ["location"]
        }
      }
    }]
  }'
```

Before this fix: HTTP 500 with `Cannot find field $defs in #/$defs/Location`.
After: HTTP 200 with a valid `tool_calls` response.

**Fix.** Build the envelope as a dict and hoist `$defs` (draft 2020-12) and
`definitions` (draft-07) from the tool's parameters to the envelope root before
calling `xgr.Grammar.from_json_schema`, so root-anchored refs resolve again. This
mirrors what the shared tool path already does (`_get_tool_schema_defs` in
`vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py`); the Cohere parser bypasses that path for its custom
tag/envelope format and had reintroduced the bug. No cross-tool merge handling is
needed here because each tool gets its own grammar. The parameters dict is copied
so the incoming request object is not mutated.

Grammars for schemas without definitions blocks are unchanged. Same bug class was
recently fixed for the GLM tool parser path in #47175 (different code path, no
overlap).

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR references #16467 or touches the Cohere parser's
tool-schema composition (checked `gh pr list` searches for "cohere defs",
"collect_tool_schema", "16467 in:body"). The nearest related work, #47175, fixes
the analogous issue in `glm47_moe_tool_parser.py`.

## Test Plan

New regression tests in `tests/reasoning/test_cohere_command_reasoning_parser.py`
(`TestCollectToolSchemaDefs`): nested-`$defs` tool through `adjust_request`,
recursive `$defs` (can never be inlined away), draft-07 `definitions`, and a
no-mutation check on the caller's parameters dict.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/reasoning/test_cohere_command_reasoning_parser.py -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/reasoning/cohere_command_reasoning_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_cohere_command_reasoning_parser.py
```

## Test Result

## Purpose
Reduce CPU time spent preprocessing images for HF-format Mistral 3 models.

This PR applies two optimizations:

  - On Transformers 5.15 and newer, call PixtralProcessor without dummy text. Image-only calls are supported there, so tokenizing generated [IMG] placeholders is unnecessary. Older Transformers versions retain the existing path.
- Use vLLM's fused mm preprocess normalization on device (introduced in #50411)

Skipping generated `[IMG]` text reduces median renderer latency from 75.1 to
69.0 ms for one image (**8.2%**) and from 310.9 to 284.0 ms for four images
(**8.7%**).

Moving rescaling and normalization to the model executor shortens the renderer's
critical path. Resizing remains in the renderer.

```text
Before: renderer: resize + normalize → executor: H2D normalized bfloat16
After:  renderer: resize + raw uint8 → executor: H2D raw uint8 + normalize
```

Setup:

- Model: `mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503`
- Input: random RGB PIL images at the default 1540x1540 size
- CPU: Intel Core i9-10920X
- Torch intra-op threads: 1, matching vLLM renderer/steady-state serving
- Transformers 5.16.1, PyTorch 2.13.0
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (CUDA 13.0)
- vLLM commit `391adf89a7`
- 5 warmup iterations followed by 40 measured iterations
- Configurations alternated during measurement
- Reported values are median latency
- Multimodal processor cache disabled


| Process and stage | 1 image before | 1 image after | 4 images before | 4 images after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Renderer: resize and prepare pixels | 68.3 ms (resize + CPU normalize) | **11.7 ms** (resize + raw `uint8`) | 232.4 ms (resize + CPU normalize) | **45.2 ms** (resize + raw `uint8`) |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Take video placeholder timestamps from the pixel path's frame sampler
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55644.

GLM-5.3-Flash video prompts are expanded by one frame sampler and encoded by another.

- **Pixels**: `Glm5NextVideoProcessor.sample_frames` samples with the checkpoint's policy — `fps_interval = 2.0`, `extract_t = int(duration * target_fps)` — and `_preprocess` pads the frame axis to a multiple of `temporal_patch_size` and divides by it to get `grid_t`.
- **Placeholders**: `Glm4vProcessingInfo._construct_video_placeholder` emits one frame of placeholders per *timestamp*, and the timestamps come from `_get_video_second_idx_glm46v`, a second sampler on GLM-4.6V's constants — `DYNAMIC_FPS_THRES = {30: 3, 300: 1, 2400: 0.5}`, `extract_t = int(duration * target_fps * temporal_patch_size)`, then `[::2]`.

`Glm5NextProcessingInfo` moved the pixel half over to the checkpoint's own processor (`get_hf_processor`, `_get_vision_info`, `_get_image_max_pixels`, `_get_video_max_pixels`) but left the timestamp half on GLM-4.6V's. The two samplers agree only for source durations between 30 s and 300 s, where `target_fps = 1` makes `duration * 1 * 2` coincide with `duration * 2`. Outside that window the prompt gets a different number of placeholders than the vision tower produces rows, the counts first meet on the GPU in `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, and the resulting error inside a worker takes the engine core down with it — one malformed request kills the server:

```
models/utils.py:709  RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [1656, 4096]
                     cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [1728, 4096]
models/utils.py:718  ValueError: Attempted to assign 1656 = 1656 multimodal tokens
                     to 1728 placeholders
...                  EngineDeadError
```

A 4 s clip at 8 fps: the pixel path picks 8 frames → `video_grid_thw` `[4, 36, 46]` → 1,656 encoder rows, while the timestamp path yields 12 timestamps → 4,968 placeholders (ratio 3). Past 300 s the error flips sign (ratio 0.5 and lower). The issue has the full sweep.

This PR overrides the timestamp computation in `Glm5NextProcessingInfo` so it samples with the video processor's own policy. The count then becomes structural rather than coincidental: one timestamp per temporal patch is exactly `grid_t` timestamps for any clip, because `_preprocess` pads the frame axis to a multiple of `temporal_patch_size` and divides by it. Only the timestamp *values* come from the sampler, and they keep the existing convention — the first frame of each temporal patch, `int(frame_index / fps)` seconds. The `do_sample_frames=False` branch (loader pre-sampled the frames) takes the count from the delivered frames and the values from `frames_indices`, so it stays exact as well.

Also folded in: a clip too short for the sampler to pick a single frame (`duration * fps_interval < 1`) currently reaches the pixel path with an empty index array and dies on an opaque `IndexError`; it is now a `ValueError` naming the clip, i.e. a rejected request.

Scope is deliberately narrow — one `ProcessingInfo` override plus a test. The issue lists two further findings (`max_pixels` never reaching the video processor, and the `{"video": 1}` supported-limit clamp) and argues that a placeholder/embedding mismatch should be a 400 rather than an engine death; those are separate changes and are not in this PR.

## Test Plan

New file `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py`. It needs no GPU and no checkpoint — both samplers and the canvas geometry are arithmetic, so the video processor is stubbed from its class defaults with `Mock(spec=...)`, as `test_glm4_1v.py` already does for `Glm4vProcessingInfo`.

For each clip it recomputes the pixel path's `video_grid_thw` (`glm_sample_frame_indices` + `smart_resize` + the `_preprocess` padding rule), then asserts `len(timestamps) == grid_t` and `len(timestamps) * tokens_per_frame == grid_t * grid_h * grid_w // merge_size ** 2`, plus that the timestamps are non-decreasing seconds within the clip. Cases:

| clip | pixel frames | `video_grid_thw` | encoder rows | timestamps before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 s @ 8 fps, 640x480 | 8 | `[4, 36, 46]` | 1,656 | 12 (4,968 placeholders) | 4 (1,656) |
| 20 s @ 30 fps, 1080p | 40 | `[20, 78, 138]` | 53,820 | 60 (161,460) | 20 (53,820) |
| 60 s @ 30 fps, 1080p | 120 | `[60, 78, 138]` | 161,460 | 60 (161,460) | 60 (161,460) |
| 301 s @ 30 fps, 720p | 602 | `[301, 42, 74]` | 233,877 | 151 (117,327) | 301 (233,877) |

The 60 s row is the regression guard: it is inside the window where the two samplers already agreed, and the count must not move. Two more tests cover the pre-sampled (`do_sample_frames=False`) branch and the too-short clip.

```bash
pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py
```

## Test Result

```
6 passed
```

Without the fix, 4 of the 6 fail (the three disagreeing clips and the too-short clip); the 60 s case passes either way, as intended.

End to end on a 3-node TP=3 deployment of `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, video prompts that previously killed the engine core on every rank now serve correctly, with `prompt_tokens` matching the arithmetic above (1,656 for the 4 s fixture); single- and multi-video prompts, mixed image+video prompts, temporal ordering in the answers, and speculative-decoding acceptance were all checked and unchanged, with no measurable throughput cost.

Lint: `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean at the pinned `v0.14.0`, plus `typos`, `check-spdx-header` and `check-root-lazy-imports`. The remaining pre-commit hooks (notably `mypy`) were not run locally — no GPU-capable build environment here.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Paged MXFP4 sparse indexer on aiter's MQA-logits kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Adds a ROCm (gfx950) path for DeepSeek V4.1's indexer with an MXFP4 K cache, built on aiter's paged MXFP4 MQA-logits Gluon kernel. The CUDA path is unchanged. There are two modes:

- **Regular MXFP4** (`indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"`): dense logits over the whole context, read straight from the paged K cache.
- **Sparse MXFP4** (opt-in, also set `indexer_sparse_logits=True`): the candidate source takes block maxima from the same pass that writes its logits, and the consumer layers score only the candidate pool instead of the whole context. Steps whose contexts are too short for the pool to pay off keep the regular pass, so it helps mainly at long contexts.

Both modes:

- The logits kernel reads the preshuffled paged K cache in place, so no K gather is needed, prefill included.
- K is written to the cache by aiter's `k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache`, and Q is quantized by `q_rope_mxfp4_quant`.
- Each prefill chunk is packed into one launch through `query_start_loc`. Uniform spec-decode steps run as `next_n`-row sequences, with the decode schedule built once per step.
- 128-token KV pages are preferred.

In sparse mode, the candidate pool is resolved once per step and shared by every consumer layer.

Requires aiter with the paged MXFP4 MQA-logits kernel and the cache ops (merged to aiter main) (https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5834)

## Tests

## Performance

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Feed parser tests and benchmarks attributed input
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

In production, the incremental decoder attributes every text chunk to the generated tokens that produced it (`DecodedText { text, attributions }`), and parsers receive those chunks. Two test paths feed parsers something else:

- The chat `roundtrip` integration test decodes token-id completions through the production decoder but forwards only `chunk.text`, and splits text-rendered completions (every HF-template model) into `DecodedText::unattributed` chunks.
- The parser benchmarks drive unified parsers through `UnifiedToolParserAdapter`, which exposes them as a `ToolParser` over `&str` chunks, with a stub tokenizer that maps every token to `u32::MAX`, and it rejects reasoning events.

Neither can exercise a parser that reads token identity, such as the token-aware Kimi K3 parser stacked on top (#58358). This PR makes both production-shaped:

- **Roundtrip:** token-id completions forward the attributed decoder chunks. Text-rendered completions are encoded and run through the production decoder too, with an assertion that the text roundtrips, and are then split at the same 7-char boundaries as before, so marker splits stay covered.
- **Benchmarks:** `benches/utils/unified.rs` adds `attributed_chunks` (decode a fixture once with special tokens, split the attributed output at chunk boundaries with `drain_prefix`) and `feed_unified_parser` (`initialize`, `parse_into`, `finish`, then text, reasoning and distinct call counts). Chunks are prepared outside the measured routine, and each fixture is checked once with real assertions, since `debug_assert!` is compiled out of bench builds. The Gemma4 benchmark moves to these helpers, `UnifiedToolParserAdapter` (its only user) is removed, and a Kimi K3 benchmark is added (mixed calls, long reasoning, long string argument, thinking prompt tail).

The current parsers match markers by spelling and ignore attributions, so parser behavior is unchanged. The benchmark numbers now include carrying attributions through the parser buffer, as production does. With the byte-level `TestTokenizer`, that is one attribution per byte, which overstates it compared with real BPE.

Landing this first gives #58358 a Kimi K3 baseline on the same harness. #58358 no longer carries its own roundtrip harness fix.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Enable fused multi-step draft decode for FlashInfer trtllm-gen
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

#46849 runs all MRV2 autoregressive draft decode steps from one metadata build in one CUDA graph when every draft attention backend opts in. FlashInfer, the default non-MLA backend on SM100, never did, so MTP and EAGLE drafters there log

```
Fused multi-step draft decode is not supported by attention backend(s) FLASHINFER; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps.
```

and rebuild metadata and replay a draft graph for each of the k−1 draft decode steps. Draft-model speculation (`method=draft_model`) does not use this loop and is unaffected.

The trtllm-gen decode metadata holds only views of buffers the fused loop keeps current (the draft `seq_lens`, advanced in place, and the block table, fixed during the loop) plus step-invariant values, and no host plan. commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Relax schema-aware tool argument conversion
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Make the shared schema-aware tool-argument conversion (`tool/parameters.rs`, used by the XML-style tool parsers: Qwen3-Coder, GLM-4.5/4.7, MiniMax M2/M3, DeepSeek DSML, and Hy) more forgiving of how models spell typed values, and stricter about composite types:

- Non-string types ignore surrounding whitespace, so `" 7 "` becomes `7` for an `integer` parameter. `string` parameters keep their text verbatim.
- Integers and numbers accept single underscores between digits (`1_000`), as Python numeric literals do.
- `"nullable": true` (the OpenAPI spelling of an optional parameter, also produced by Transformers' `get_json_schema`) adds `null` to the accepted types.
- `object` / `array` parameters only accept JSON that decodes to that type. Previously `"5"` for an `object` parameter became the number `5`, and `"[1]"` became an array; such values now stay strings, and unions such as `["object", "array"]` still pick the matching member.

This is the bottom of a stack; the `hf` response-template parser above it (#59005) reuses this conversion, so all Rust tool parsers share one set of argument-typing rules instead of each following a different reference implementation.

No open PR covers this conversion.

cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat --test roundtrip --no-fail-fast

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Engram] Keep THP tables private when resolving shared memory
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`use_thp` is silently ignored under DP. It is only validated against `dp_shared_memory` at construction, where the field is still unset. The DP default from #57651 then resolves sharing on for any CPU-offloaded, non-elastic run with DP > 1, and the table allocator takes the shared branch before the THP branch added in #56926:

```python
config = EngramConfig(use_thp=True)  # dp_shared_memory=None
config.resolve_dp_shared_memory(ParallelConfig(data_parallel_size=2))
config.dp_shared_memory  # True on main; the tables are never THP-backed
```

This PR leaves automatic sharing off when THP is requested (one added predicate, `and not self.use_thp`). That is what both fields already document: sharing defaults on "whenever the other settings allow it", and `use_thp` "requires cpu_offload without dp_shared_memory".

Effect on a DP > 1 run with `use_thp=True`: instead of one `/dev/shm` table shared by the node-local replicas, the tables are private, THP-backed and head-sharded across the node-local Engram DP group, which is the existing non-shared path. Host memory stays at one table per node (without co-located replicas, sharing was not possible anyway); lookups use the per-step Engram DP collectives that sharing avoids. THP versus shared-table performance under DP has not been measured here. Users who prefer sharing can leave `use_thp` unset.

Unchanged: every configuration without `use_thp`, explicit `dp_shared_memory=False`, and the construction-time rejection of explicit `use_thp=True, dp_shared_memory=True`.

Not a duplicate: open PR searches for `use_thp`, `dp_shared_memory`, `resolve_dp_shared_memory` and Engram THP found no fix for this interaction. #58439 adds a `checkpoint_mapped` predicate to the same expression for a different option; whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase.

## Test Plan

The existing resolver test matrix now also covers implicit THP, explicit private tables and elastic EP. A new test checks that explicit shared memory plus THP is still rejected. Both are pure config tests and use the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker, so their teardown does not need an accelerator.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \
  -k 'engram_dp_shared_memory_defaults or engram_thp_rejects_explicit_shared_memory'
```

## Test Result

Against main `6b24bd8e75a3e465083e8a131968915bc00efaf4`, running the new tests on the original and on the fixed `vllm/config/engram.py`:

```text
Original: 1 failed, 6 passed   (only the implicit THP case fails)
Fixed:    7 passed

```

The tests ran in a CPU-only container (Python 3.12.13, pytest 9.1.1), with no config mocks or custom pytest plugin. Ruff 0.14.0 check and format passed.

No model evaluation: the change only selects which existing storage path holds the tables and does not change lookup results. The THP storage path and its exact-row lookups are covered by #56926's tests.

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

 This PR supersedes #54234 with an implementation based on the shared ParserEngine.


Add reasoning and tool-call parsing support for PLaMo 3 through the shared `ParserEngine`, registered as both `--reasoning-parser plamo3` and `--tool-call-parser plamo3`. 

PLaMo 3 emits reasoning and tool calls with nested control markers:

```text
<|plamo:begin_tool_requests:plamo|>
<|plamo:begin_tool_request:plamo|>
<|plamo:begin_tool_name:plamo|>get_weather<|plamo:end_tool_name:plamo|>
<|plamo:begin_tool_arguments:plamo|><|plamo:constrain|>json<|plamo:msg|>{"city":"Tokyo"}<|plamo:end_tool_arguments:plamo|>
<|plamo:end_tool_request:plamo|>
<|plamo:begin_tool_request:plamo|>
...
<|plamo:end_tool_request:plamo|>
<|plamo:end_tool_requests:plamo|>
```

This PR adds:

- a declarative PLaMo 3 parser configuration and thin reasoning/tool-parser adapters, with custom handling for multi-token tags; and
- xgrammar support through a PLaMo 3 structural-tag grammar and custom-tokenizer initialization, including parallel tool calls and `auto`, `required`, and named tool choices.

PLaMo3 parser needs a few model-specific adaptations:

- `ParserEngine` does not yet handle multi-token reasoning tags generically, so PLaMo 3 overrides the relevant helpers to recognize complete tags, preserve their special-token fragments, and remove incomplete suffixes when generation is cut off. If another family such as Kimi K2 needs the same behavior in the future, this can be promoted into a shared parser-engine mechanism.
- PLaMo 3 tool names and arguments may be flushed together at the end of generation, so its event conversion preserves the first argument delta. Its vLLM-owned structural-tag grammar also models the native nested request blocks and their empty separator directly.

Note:
- `TokenizerInfo.from_huggingface()` normally builds xgrammar metadata for Hugging Face fast, tiktoken, and SentencePiece tokenizers, but it rejects PLaMo 3's custom numba-based tokenizer. PLaMo 3 therefore uses its existing `init_xgrammar()` integration hook, which is also used by SGLang and supplies equivalent byte-fallback vocabulary and stop-token metadata. This path is restricted to `model_type == "plamo3"`; other models continue to use `from_huggingface()`.

## Purpose

`LLM.encode()` writes its internal pooling task into the caller's `PoolingParams`. Reusing `PoolingParams(use_activation=False)` first with an `embed` LLM and later with a separate `token_embed` LLM fails before inference:

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Detect the CUDA toolkit the way FlashInfer does in has_flashinfer()
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

When `flashinfer-cubin` is not installed, `has_flashinfer()` treats FlashInfer as unusable unless `nvcc` is on `PATH`. FlashInfer's own JIT (`jit/cpp_ext.py::get_cuda_path`) looks further: `$CUDA_HOME`, then `$CUDA_PATH`, then `nvcc` on `PATH`, then `/usr/local/cuda`.

On a bare-metal or SLURM host the toolkit usually sits at `/usr/local/cuda` without being on `PATH`. There, every `has_flashinfer()`-gated kernel is silently disabled (TRTLLM/CUTLASS MoE, FlashInfer FP8/NVFP4 linears, AllReduce+RMSNorm fusion), and only a `debug_once` line is logged. FlashInfer attention is not gated by `has_flashinfer()`, so on the same host it keeps JIT-compiling with that toolkit. Setting `CUDA_HOME` does not help on main either.

This PR:
- mirrors FlashInfer's toolkit lookup without importing FlashInfer, since importing it initializes CUDA;
- also requires `ninja` on `PATH`, because FlashInfer runs it from there and a non-activated venv lacks it;
- replaces the `debug_once` with a `warning_once` that points to `CUDA_HOME` or `flashinfer download-kernels`.

## Test Plan

- GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13.1 at `/usr/local/cuda`, no flashinfer-cubin.
- E2E: two venvs from the same precompiled wheel, main `a9f07d0bc5` (FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1) and this PR on top of it. `nvcc` is off `PATH` and `CUDA_HOME` is unset in all arms. Same node, interleaved rounds, fresh server per arm.
- Unit tests and probe: re-run after rebasing onto main `94d1462924` (FlashInfer 0.7.0).

```bash
pytest tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py
vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 32768 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-prefix-caching
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1000 \
  --random-output-len 1000 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --max-concurrency {1,32}
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests:** both new tests pass. On main both fail: the first because `has_flashinfer()` returns False, the second because it returns True. (Run unmodified, they error in the fixture, since `_DEFAULT_CUDA_HOME` does not exist on main.)

**Toolkit probe** (FlashInfer 0.7.0; "can JIT" is FlashInfer's own `get_cuda_path()` plus `ninja` on `PATH`):

| environment | FlashInfer can JIT | main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| toolkit only at `/usr/local/cuda` | yes | **False** | True |
| `CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda` | yes | **False** | True |
| `CUDA_HOME=/nonexistent`, nvcc on `PATH` | no | **True** | False + warning |
| runtime image (no `bin/nvcc`) | no | False | False + warning |
| nvcc on `PATH`, venv not activated (no `ninja`) | no | **True** | False + warning |

**Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP1, 3 rounds.** MoE backend is Triton on main; FlashInfer TRTLLM with this PR and with `PATH` fixed by hand.

| | main | PR | main + `/usr/local/cuda/bin` on `PATH` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| c=1 output tok/s | 274.4 ± 0.4 | **309.1** ± 1.1 (+12.6%, t = 51) | 308.4 ± 1.2 |
| c=32 output tok/s | 3312 ± 20 | **3808** ± 2 (+15.0%, t = 42) | 3813 ± 5 |
| GSM8K | 0.854 | 0.847 | 0.846 |

The PR matches the `PATH` workaround within noise, so the gain comes from the FlashInfer kernels being re-enabled. The GSM8K gap to main is the MoE kernel change and is within one standard error (≈1 pp).

**Supporting data: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8, TP2, 2 rounds.** Main falls back to DeepGEMM MoE with no AR fusion; the PR uses TRTLLM MoE with AR+RMSNorm fusion.

- The warning now fires on every CUDA install that has neither flashinfer-cubin nor a usable toolkit. On main such installs log only at debug level.
